+# PeTTaChainer chaining verdict at pinned shas
+
+**Status: backward chaining is BROKEN. Forward chaining WORKS.** Verified
+2026-07-28 at PeTTaChainer@02a85c6 + PeTTa@43705f5.
+
+The April 2026 blocker ("PeTTaChainer backward chaining returns empty for all
+queries, including its own test suite") is **not fixed**. It reproduces at
+upstream HEAD, in upstream's own isolated task environment, against upstream's
+own tests. Forward chaining, by contrast, is sound and answers the ProofWriter
+probe correctly — but only under a rule encoding that neither of PeTTaChainer's
+LLM-facing specs documents.
+
+Upstream issue: https://github.com/rTreutlein/PeTTaChainer/issues/1
+
+## Pins
+
+| Component | Repo | SHA | Date |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| PeTTaChainer | `rTreutlein/PeTTaChainer` | `02a85c63be6a735f50f50e1084a717b3256b8406` | 2026-07-20 |
+| PeTTa | `trueagi-io/PeTTa` (= `patham9/PeTTa`) | `43705f5d9ff8958ffe7f0aa6777fb8477f2401f2` | 2026-07-24 |
+
+Both were `main` HEAD on 2026-07-28, so this is the pair a fresh install per
+PeTTaChainer's README gets today. PeTTa is `pins.env`'s `PETTA_SHA`;
+PeTTaChainer is pinned in `tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh` (see
+`pins.env`'s trailing note on why it is not vendored repo-wide).
+
+Environment: PeTTaChainer's own `.myclaw/Dockerfile` — `swipl:9.3.33`,
+CPython 3.10.18, `janus-swi` 1.5.2 compiled in-image, `uv sync --frozen`.
+
+## Verdict per chaining mode
+
+### Backward chaining (`query`) — BROKEN
+
+`query` returns empty for **every** query, including a query for a fact that is
+demonstrably in the KB. No error, no warning, no timeout — a silent empty
+result. Three lines reproduce it
+(`tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/minimal_repro.metta`):
+
+```metta
+!(import! &self petta_chainer)
+!(compileadd mk (: f1 (Dog fido) (STV 1.0 1.0)))
+!(match &kb ($t (mk MAIN Nil) $prf $tv) ($t $prf $tv))   ; -> ((Dog fido) f1 (STV 1.0 1.0))
+!(query 100 mk (: $prf (Dog fido) $tv))                  ; -> nothing
+```
+
+`compileadd` works: the statement is accepted, the fact lands in the KB, and the
+compiled rules are emitted. Only retrieval through `query` is dead. Raising the
+step budget does not help — 1, 2, 4, 100 and 1000 all return empty.
+
+This is more general than April recorded. April's note was "returns empty for
+all queries"; the direct-fact case shows the backward chainer fails before any
+inference is required.
+
+### Forward chaining (`forward-chain`) — WORKS
+
+Forward chaining derives correctly and the derived facts land in the KB with
+sensible truth values:
+
+```
+!(forward-chain 10 ck (sel ck (A)))
+-> (((B) (ck MAIN Nil) (r1 a0) (STV 1.0 0.8999189847918079)))
+```
+
+A forward-derived fact is **not** retrievable by `query` afterwards — same bug
+as above, which is why upstream's `test_forward_chain_derives_fact_visible_to_
+backward_query` fails at its final assertion rather than its first.
+
+### Rule truth-value encoding — a second, independent defect
+
+An `Implication` carrying `(STV s c)` compiles without error and then **never
+fires — in either chaining mode**. The same rule carrying
+`(CTV (STV s c) (STV s c))` forward-chains normally.
+`tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/rule_tv_encoding.metta` shows both side by side:
+
+| Rule TV on the Implication | `forward-chain` result |
+|---|---|
+| `(STV 1.0 0.9)` | `()` — rule inert |
+| `(CTV (STV 1.0 1.0) (STV 0.0 1.0))` | `(((B) (ck MAIN Nil) (r1 a0) (STV 1.0 0.899...)))` |
+
+The `STV` form is a **supported** form, not a deprecated one:
+`pettachainer/metta/tests/test_stv_implication_derived_ctv.metta` exists
+precisely to assert that an `(STV 0.6 0.9)` Implication derives its conclusion
+at `(STV 0.6 0.8999998649685302)`. Re-running that test's exact shape through
+`forward-chain` derives nothing, so the form is broken in the forward path too —
+this is not merely the backward-chaining bug seen through that test.
+
+It is also the **documented** form: `LLM_RULE_SPEC.md`'s "Rule Template" section
+writes rules with `(STV 1.0 1.0)`, and neither `LLM_RULE_SPEC.md` nor
+`LANGUAGE_SPEC.md` mentions `CTV` at all — while every other file under
+`pettachainer/metta/tests/` uses `CTV`. `LLM_RULE_SPEC.md` is what
+`get_language_spec()` hands an LLM, so a semantic parser following the spec
+exactly emits rules that silently do nothing.
+
+The compiled output suggests where it goes: the `STV` form compiles to a rule
+whose CTV is derived at run time from KB base rates for the premise and
+conclusion (`FoldAllCompiled ... BaseRateEvidence 0.0 0.0` →
+`ImplicationCTVFormula`), which yields nothing on a KB with no prior evidence
+for the conclusion.
+
+This is a fresh instance of the silent-failure class the April attempt logged
+(`notes/stall-ledger.md` S3, `docs/april-findings.md`): wrong encoding →
+empty result → no error.
+
+## Upstream test suites, verbatim
+
+Both are upstream's own suites, run by upstream's own runners, in upstream's own
+container.
+
+### Python: `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests`
+
+```
+test_acceptance_game_scores_downstream_goal_not_estimate_table ... ERROR
+test_contract_value_uses_hidden_game_payoff ... ok
+test_pettachainer_accepts_profitable_contracts_from_goal_truth ... ERROR
+test_query_path_uses_accept_contract_goal ... ok
+test_all_facts_supports_full_kb_forward_chaining ... FAIL
+test_default_logic_keeps_pln_or_semantics ... ok
+test_forward_chain_accepts_canonical_facts ... FAIL
+test_forward_chain_derives_fact_visible_to_backward_query ... FAIL
+test_forward_chain_outputs_can_seed_the_next_run ... ok
+test_predicate_logic_config_or_introduction ... FAIL
+test_select_facts_builds_an_initial_forward_seed ... FAIL
+test_select_facts_rejects_a_missing_seed ... ok
+test_check_query_accepts_inner_form ... ok
+test_check_query_rejects_invalid_forms ... ok
+test_check_stmt_accepts_supported_forms ... ok
+test_check_stmt_rejects_invalid_forms ... ok
+
+Ran 16 tests in 0.456s
+FAILED (failures=5, errors=2)
+```
+
+All five `FAIL`s are `AssertionError: [] is not true` on a `query` result. Both
+`ERROR`s are `RuntimeError: PeTTaChainer returned no accept decision for
+contractReliable`, raised because a `query` came back empty. In the four
+forward-chaining tests the forward assertion (`assertIn("Path A C", ...)`)
+passes and only the following `query` assertion fails — forward derives, the
+query cannot see it. Full log: `results/ptc-verdict/python-unittest.log`.
+
+### MeTTa: `cd pettachainer/metta && ./test.sh`
+
+```
+FAIL tests/test.metta                              FAIL tests/test_math.metta
+FAIL tests/test_backward_dag_helpers.metta         FAIL tests/test_member_compat.metta
+FAIL tests/test_backward_open_query_results.metta  PASS tests/test_member_concept_node.metta
+FAIL tests/test_base_rate_cache.metta              FAIL tests/test_merged_subgoal_rule_application.metta
+FAIL tests/test_benchgen_metta.metta               FAIL tests/test_nary_conjuction.metta
+FAIL tests/test_best_first_runtime.metta           FAIL tests/test_negated_evidence_merge.metta
+PASS tests/test_chainer_add_atom.metta             FAIL tests/test_numeric_pattern_dist.metta
+PASS tests/test_dispatch_determinism.metta         FAIL tests/test_particle_values.metta
+FAIL tests/test_distribution_values.metta          FAIL tests/test_query_adds.metta
+FAIL tests/test_evidence_semantics.metta           FAIL tests/test_query_compute_in_compound.metta
+FAIL tests/test_foldall_merged_outputs.metta       FAIL tests/test_query_materialize.metta
+FAIL tests/test_foldall_query_goal.metta           FAIL tests/test_rectangle_area.metta
+FAIL tests/test_forward_backward_compose.metta     FAIL tests/test_specializing_rule.metta
+PASS tests/test_forward_chainer.metta              FAIL tests/test_stv_implication_derived_ctv.metta
+FAIL tests/test_forward_incremental_base_rates.metta  FAIL tests/test_total_implication_aggregate.metta
+FAIL tests/test_frontier_pooling.metta             PASS tests/test_uniform_prior.metta
+FAIL tests/test_height_average.metta               FAIL tests/test_var_head.metta
+FAIL tests/test_idealized_confidence.metta         PASS examples/base_rate_acceptance_game_libpln.metta
+FAIL tests/test_implication_inversion.metta        FAIL examples/base_rate_acceptance_game_pettachainer.metta
+FAIL tests/test_implication_premise.metta          FAIL examples/deductionrevision.metta
+FAIL tests/test_inheritance_aggregate_cycle.metta  FAIL examples/direct.metta
+FAIL tests/test_inheritance_query_proof.metta      FAIL examples/flyingraven.metta
+FAIL tests/test_lifting_merge.metta                FAIL examples/raveninduction.metta
+FAIL tests/test_logic_config.metta                 FAIL examples/raveninduction_implication_pettachainer.metta
+                                                   FAIL examples/smokes.metta
+                                                   FAIL examples/toothbrush.metta
+
+Summary: 6 passed, 44 failed
+```
+
+(Two columns for width; the log lists them in one column.)
+
+The split is almost exactly "uses `query` or not": **none** of the 6 passing
+files calls `query`, and **43 of the 44** failing files do. The single exception
+is `test_backward_dag_helpers.metta`, which fails on a truth-value mismatch
+(`is 1.0, should 0.8999975376989856`) in a backward-chaining helper — a
+different symptom in the same subsystem.
+
+`test_forward_backward_compose.metta`, the file April named, fails exactly as
+April described:
+
+```
+is (), should ().                                             ✅
+is (), should (: (r2 (r1 a0)) (Goal) (STV 1.0 0.999700089898053)).  ❌
+```
+
+Full log: `results/ptc-verdict/metta-testsh.log`.
+
+## April format-A probe
+
+`docs/april-findings.md`'s "Translation A" ProofWriter example — theory
+RelNoneg-OWA-D1-390 as 7 facts + 3 rules, type definitions excluded — run
+through `compileadd` and then the findings table's questions, under both modes
+and both rule encodings. Script: `tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/proofwriter_format_a.py`.
+Answer mapping is the findings doc's OWA rule (query the positive form; empty →
+Unknown).
+
+| Question | Gold | Backward (`stv`) | Backward (`ctv`) | Forward (`stv`) | Forward (`ctv`) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| The cow needs the bear. | True | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | True ✓ | True ✓ |
+| The cow does not need the bear. | False | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | False ✓ | False ✓ |
+| The cow likes the squirrel. | True | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | True ✓ |
+| The cow does not like the squirrel. | False | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | Unknown ✗ | False ✓ |
+| The bear does not like the squirrel. | Unknown | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ |
+| The dog likes the bear. | Unknown | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ | Unknown ✓ |
+| | | **2/6** | **2/6** | **4/6** | **6/6** |
+
+Read the backward columns as 0/6, not 2/6: every query returned empty, so the
+two "correct" rows are correct only because empty *is* the Unknown answer. A
+chainer that always returns empty scores 2/6 on this table by construction.
+
+Forward chaining with `ctv` rules is **6/6**, including the depth-1 derivation:
+
+```
++ ((Like cow_1 squirrel_1) (kb... MAIN Nil) (round_likes_squirrel cow_is_round) (STV 1.0 0.8999189847918079))
+```
+
+Forward chaining with `stv` rules — the encoding the April semantic-parser
+emitted, per `LLM_RULE_SPEC.md` — derives nothing, so it gets the two depth-0
+questions right from the asserted facts and both depth-1 questions wrong.
+
+Full log: `results/ptc-verdict/format-a-probe.log`.
+
+## What this rules out
+
+- **Not a PeTTa regression.** The same failure reproduces against PeTTa@d9a437c
+  (2026-07-20, contemporaneous with the PeTTaChainer pin), so PeTTa's PR #212
+  quoting change — the one that broke `PLN/examples/Direct.metta`
+  (`docs/known-issues.md` #2) — is not the cause.
+- **Not a SWI-Prolog version artifact.** Reproduces on swipl 9.3.33 (in the
+  container) and swipl 10.1.5 (on the host).
+- **Not a locale artifact.** All runs export `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`
+  (`docs/known-issues.md` #1).
+- **Not our environment.** Upstream's own `.myclaw` task environment, built from
+  upstream's own Dockerfile, running upstream's own test commands.
+- **Not API misuse.** Upstream's own tests fail the same way, and the failure
+  reproduces at the MeTTa level with no Python in the path.
+
+## Why the `Direct.metta` finding was not filed alongside
+
+`docs/known-issues.md` #2 (PLN's `examples/Direct.metta` stale vs PeTTa's current
+quoting convention) was held back from the PeTTaChainer issue on purpose. It
+belongs to `trueagi-io/PLN`, whose `Direct.metta` is authored by Patrick Hammer
+and Peter Isaev; PeTTaChainer's maintainer has one commit in that repo. The
+maintainer sets do not meaningfully overlap, so bundling the two would have put
+an off-topic PLN item into a PeTTaChainer bug report rather than making one
+conversation out of two. `Direct.metta` goes to the PLN consults through the
+operator's channel instead.
+
+## Consequence for this repo
+
+The pipeline arm (ROADMAP Goal 1: semantic-parser → PeTTaChainer) **cannot use
+backward chaining** at these pins. Two things follow:
+
+1. The `lib_pln` arm stays the ProofWriter path of record. Nothing here changes
+   `docs/conventions.md`.
+2. If the pipeline arm proceeds against PeTTaChainer before an upstream fix, it
+   must be forward-chaining-only *and* emit `CTV`-wrapped rules — which means
+   the semantic-parser cannot use `get_language_spec()`'s rule template
+   unmodified. That is a real constraint, not a workaround preference: the
+   documented template produces inert rules.
+
+## Reproducing
+
+```bash
+bash tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh
+```
+
+Clones both pins from the sibling offline `deps/` bundles into `vendor/`, builds PeTTaChainer's `.myclaw` image, and
+writes five logs to `results/ptc-verdict/`. Needs podman (or docker), git, and
+the sibling `deps/` directory; nothing else — SWI-Prolog, Python, janus and uv all
+come from the image. Takes roughly ten minutes cold, most of it the image build.
+See `tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/README.md` for what each log should contain.
+
+## Revision record
+
+- 2026-07-28 — first issue, task `ptc-revalidate`.

+# ptc-revalidate repro
+
+Evidence behind `docs/ptc-verdict.md`: does PeTTaChainer chain at the pinned
+shas? Answer, 2026-07-28: forward yes, backward no.
+
+Run everything:
+
+```bash
+bash tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh
+```
+
+Needs podman (or docker), git, and the sibling `deps/` bundle directory. SWI-Prolog, Python,
+janus and uv come from PeTTaChainer's own `.myclaw` image, so the host toolchain
+does not affect the result. Set `CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker` to force an engine.
+Roughly ten minutes cold, most of it the image build; re-runs are much faster
+(two named volumes, `plnbench-ptc-uv-cache` and `plnbench-ptc-uv-python`, keep
+uv's cache and its managed CPython).
+
+The script always exits 0. The upstream suites are *expected* to fail at these
+pins — that is the finding, not a broken run.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | What it is |
+|---|---|
+| `run-verdict.sh` | driver: fetch pins, build image, run all five probes |
+| `minimal_repro.metta` | 3 lines: a fact is in the KB, `query` cannot find it |
+| `rule_tv_encoding.metta` | an `(STV s c)` Implication is inert; `(CTV ...)` fires |
+| `proofwriter_format_a.py` | the April ProofWriter probe, both modes, both encodings |
+
+## What the logs should say
+
+Written to `results/ptc-verdict/` (gitignored — regenerate, don't commit).
+
+| Log | Expected at PeTTaChainer@02a85c6 + PeTTa@43705f5 |
+|---|---|
+| `image-build.log` | `Successfully tagged localhost/plnbench-ptc:02a85c6` |
+| `python-unittest.log` | `Ran 16 tests` / `FAILED (failures=5, errors=2)`; every failure is `[] is not true` on a `query` |
+| `metta-testsh.log` | `Summary: 6 passed, 44 failed`; no passing file calls `query` |
+| `minimal-repro.log` | the `match` line prints the fact, the `query` line prints nothing |
+| `rule-tv-encoding.log` | stv forward-chain `()`, ctv forward-chain derives `(B)`, ctv `query` still empty, upstream's stv-test shape forward-chains to `()` |
+| `format-a-probe.log` | backward 0/6 (all empty), forward+ctv 6/6, forward+stv 4/6 |
+
+Anything else means the pins moved or the environment differs — check the pins
+printed at the top of the run before reading the logs as a new finding.
+
+## Pins
+
+PeTTa comes from `pins.env` (`PETTA_SHA`). PeTTaChainer is pinned inside
+`run-verdict.sh` (`PETTACHAINER_SHA=02a85c6...`), not in `pins.env`, per
+`pins.env`'s trailing note: vendoring the pipeline arm's subjects repo-wide
+would bake in an arm that has not been validated. Bumping either pin means
+re-running this and revising `docs/ptc-verdict.md` — the verdict is only about
+the shas it names.

+; Minimal repro: PeTTaChainer backward chaining (`query`) returns empty for a
+; fact that is demonstrably in the KB.
+;
+; Run with CWD = <PeTTaChainer>/pettachainer/metta so `petta_chainer` resolves:
+;   cd <PeTTaChainer>/pettachainer/metta && petta <path-to-this-file>
+;
+; Expected (a working backward chainer): the `query` line prints the compiled
+; fact, e.g. (: f1 (Dog fido) (STV 1.0 1.0)).
+; Observed at PeTTaChainer@02a85c6 + PeTTa@43705f5: the `match` line finds the
+; fact, the `query` line prints nothing, and no error is raised.
+
+!(import! &self petta_chainer)
+
+!(compileadd mk (: f1 (Dog fido) (STV 1.0 1.0)))
+
+; The fact is in the KB -- this prints ((Dog fido) f1 (STV 1.0 1.0)).
+!("--- match &kb: is the fact there? ---")
+!(match &kb ($t (mk MAIN Nil) $prf $tv) ($t $prf $tv))
+
+; Backward chaining for that same fact -- this prints nothing.
+!("--- query: can backward chaining find it? ---")
+!(query 100 mk (: $prf (Dog fido) $tv))
+
+!("--- end ---")

+"""April 2026 ProofWriter format-A probe, re-run against pinned PeTTaChainer.
+
+Reproduces docs/april-findings.md "Translation A: semantic-parser (hyphen) format":
+the RelNoneg-OWA-D1-390 theory as 7 facts + 3 rules (type definitions excluded --
+PeTTaChainer's add_atom rejects them), then the True/Unknown questions from the
+findings table, under both chaining modes.
+
+Answer mapping is the findings doc's OWA rule: query the POSITIVE form of the
+statement; a non-empty proof means the positive holds (question positive -> True,
+question negated -> False); an empty result means Unknown.
+
+Two rule encodings are probed because the two upstream specs disagree:
+  stv -- (STV 1.0 0.9) on the Implication, as pettachainer/LLM_RULE_SPEC.md's
+         rule template writes it and as the semantic-parser emitted in April.
+  ctv -- (CTV (STV 1.0 1.0) (STV 0.0 1.0)) on the Implication, as every test in
+         pettachainer/metta/tests/ writes it.
+Running both keeps an empty result from being blamed on the encoding.
+
+Usage: python proofwriter_format_a.py [--steps N]
+Exit code 0 always -- this is a probe that reports, not a test that judges.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+
+from pettachainer import PeTTaChainer
+
+FACTS = [
+    "(: bear_likes_dog      (Like bear_1 dog_1)         (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: cow_is_round        (HasAttribute cow_1 round)  (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: cow_likes_bear      (Like cow_1 bear_1)         (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: cow_needs_bear      (Need cow_1 bear_1)         (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: dog_needs_squirrel  (Need dog_1 squirrel_1)     (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: dog_sees_cow        (See dog_1 cow_1)           (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+    "(: squirrel_needs_dog  (Need squirrel_1 dog_1)     (STV 1.0 0.9))",
+]
+
+# (name, premises, conclusion) -- the tv wrapper is filled in per encoding.
+RULES = [
+    (
+        "round_likes_squirrel",
+        "(HasAttribute $x round)",
+        "(Like $x squirrel_1)",
+    ),
+    (
+        "bear_round_squirrel_needs",
+        "(HasAttribute bear_1 round) (Like bear_1 squirrel_1)",
+        "(Need squirrel_1 bear_1)",
+    ),
+    (
+        "cow_needs_dog_cold",
+        "(Need cow_1 dog_1)",
+        "(HasAttribute cow_1 cold)",
+    ),
+]
+
+RULE_TV = {
+    "stv": "(STV 1.0 0.9)",
+    "ctv": "(CTV (STV 1.0 1.0) (STV 0.0 1.0))",
+}
+
+# Every question in the findings table, mapped to the positive form that is
+# actually queried. "expected" is the ProofWriter gold answer.
+QUESTIONS = [
+    ("The cow needs the bear.", "(Need cow_1 bear_1)", False, "True", 0),
+    ("The cow does not need the bear.", "(Need cow_1 bear_1)", True, "False", 0),
+    ("The cow likes the squirrel.", "(Like cow_1 squirrel_1)", False, "True", 1),
+    ("The cow does not like the squirrel.", "(Like cow_1 squirrel_1)", True, "False", 1),
+    ("The bear does not like the squirrel.", "(Like bear_1 squirrel_1)", True, "Unknown", 1),
+    ("The dog likes the bear.", "(Like dog_1 bear_1)", False, "Unknown", 0),
+]
+
+
+def rules_for(encoding):
+    tv = RULE_TV[encoding]
+    return [
+        f"(: {name} (Implication (Premises {premises}) (Conclusions {conclusion})) {tv})"
+        for name, premises, conclusion in RULES
+    ]
+
+
+def answer_from(proofs, negated):
+    """Findings-doc OWA mapping: empty -> Unknown, otherwise the positive holds."""
+    if not proofs:
+        return "Unknown"
+    return "False" if negated else "True"
+
+
+def load(encoding):
+    handler = PeTTaChainer()
+    for atom in FACTS:
+        handler.add_atom(atom)
+    for atom in rules_for(encoding):
+        handler.add_atom(atom)
+    return handler
+
+
+def probe_backward(encoding, steps):
+    """Backward chaining only: compileadd, then query."""
+    handler = load(encoding)
+    rows = []
+    for question, positive, negated, expected, depth in QUESTIONS:
+        proofs = handler.query(f"(: $prf {positive} $tv)", steps=steps, timeout_sec=0)
+        proofs = [str(p) for p in proofs]
+        rows.append({
+            "question": question,
+            "queried": positive,
+            "depth": depth,
+            "expected": expected,
+            "got": answer_from(proofs, negated),
+            "proofs": proofs,
+        })
+    return rows
+
+
+def probe_forward(encoding, steps):
+    """Forward chaining: saturate from the whole KB, then read the derived facts.
+
+    The forward verdict is whether the conclusion appears among the canonical
+    facts after saturation -- a check that does not route through query() and so
+    stays independent of the backward path. The query column is reported too, to
+    show whether a forward-derived fact becomes visible to a backward query.
+    """
+    handler = load(encoding)
+    derived = [str(f) for f in handler.forward_chain(handler.all_facts(), steps=steps)]
+    all_facts = [str(f) for f in handler.all_facts()]
+    rows = []
+    for question, positive, negated, expected, depth in QUESTIONS:
+        # Match on the surface term: a canonical fact prints as
+        # "(: (kb MAIN Nil) <proof> (Like cow_1 squirrel_1) (STV ...))".
+        in_kb = any(positive in fact for fact in all_facts)
+        proofs = handler.query(f"(: $prf {positive} $tv)", steps=steps, timeout_sec=0)
+        proofs = [str(p) for p in proofs]
+        rows.append({
+            "question": question,
+            "queried": positive,
+            "depth": depth,
+            "expected": expected,
+            "got": "True" if in_kb and not negated else ("False" if in_kb else "Unknown"),
+            "derived_into_kb": in_kb,
+            "query_after_forward": proofs,
+        })
+    return {"derived": derived, "facts_after": all_facts, "rows": rows}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=100)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    report = {"steps": args.steps, "encodings": {}}
+    for encoding in ("stv", "ctv"):
+        backward = probe_backward(encoding, args.steps)
+        forward = probe_forward(encoding, args.steps)
+        report["encodings"][encoding] = {"backward": backward, "forward": forward}
+
+        print(f"\n=== encoding={encoding}  rule tv {RULE_TV[encoding]} ===")
+        print("--- backward chaining (query only) ---")
+        for row in backward:
+            mark = "match" if row["got"] == row["expected"] else "MISMATCH"
+            print(f"  [{mark:8}] expected={row['expected']:7} got={row['got']:7} "
+                  f"d={row['depth']} {row['question']}")
+            for proof in row["proofs"]:
+                print(f"             proof: {proof}")
+        print(f"--- forward chaining (saturate, then read kb) ---")
+        print(f"  derived {len(forward['derived'])} new canonical fact(s)")
+        for fact in forward["derived"]:
+            print(f"    + {fact}")
+        for row in forward["rows"]:
+            mark = "match" if row["got"] == row["expected"] else "MISMATCH"
+            print(f"  [{mark:8}] expected={row['expected']:7} got={row['got']:7} "
+                  f"in_kb={row['derived_into_kb']} query_after={row['query_after_forward']} "
+                  f"{row['question']}")
+
+    json.dump(report, sys.stdout, indent=2)
+    print()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/rule_tv_encoding.metta b/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/rule_tv_encoding.metta
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..93d9073
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/rule_tv_encoding.metta
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+; Companion repro: an Implication carrying (STV s c) compiles without error but
+; never fires under forward chaining. The same rule carrying
+; (CTV (STV ...) (STV ...)) fires normally.
+;
+; The STV form is supported upstream, not deprecated:
+; pettachainer/metta/tests/test_stv_implication_derived_ctv.metta asserts that an
+; (STV 0.6 0.9) Implication derives its conclusion. It is also the form
+; LLM_RULE_SPEC.md's "Rule Template" section documents -- neither that file nor
+; LANGUAGE_SPEC.md mentions CTV, while every other file in
+; pettachainer/metta/tests/ uses it.
+;
+; Run with CWD = <PeTTaChainer>/pettachainer/metta:
+;   cd <PeTTaChainer>/pettachainer/metta && petta <path-to-this-file>
+;
+; Observed at PeTTaChainer@02a85c6 + PeTTa@43705f5:
+;   stv forward-chain -> ()                                     (rule inert)
+;   ctv forward-chain -> (((B) (ck MAIN Nil) (r1 a0) (STV ...))) (rule fires)
+;   ctv query for (B) -> nothing, even though (B) is now a KB fact
+;                                                    (the backward-chaining bug)
+
+!(import! &self petta_chainer)
+
+; The canonical-fact selector, copied from
+; pettachainer/metta/tests/test_forward_backward_compose.metta.
+(= (sel $kb $type)
+   (collapse
+      (once
+         (match &kb
+            ($type ($kb MAIN Nil) $prf $tv)
+            ($type ($kb MAIN Nil) $prf $tv)))))
+
+!("=== rule tv (STV 1.0 0.9) -- LLM_RULE_SPEC.md rule template form ===")
+!(compileadd sk (: a0 (A) (STV 1.0 0.9)))
+!(compileadd sk (: r1 (Implication (Premises (A)) (Conclusions (B))) (STV 1.0 0.9)))
+!("--- forward-chain: derived facts ---")
+!(forward-chain 10 sk (sel sk (A)))
+!("--- kb contents after forward-chain ---")
+!(match &kb ($t (sk MAIN Nil) $prf $tv) ($t $prf $tv))
+
+!("=== rule tv (CTV (STV 1.0 1.0) (STV 0.0 1.0)) -- tests/ form ===")
+!(compileadd ck (: a0 (A) (STV 1.0 0.9)))
+!(compileadd ck (: r1 (Implication (Premises (A)) (Conclusions (B))) (CTV (STV 1.0 1.0) (STV 0.0 1.0))))
+!("--- forward-chain: derived facts ---")
+!(forward-chain 10 ck (sel ck (A)))
+!("--- kb contents after forward-chain ---")
+!(match &kb ($t (ck MAIN Nil) $prf $tv) ($t $prf $tv))
+!("--- query for the forward-derived (B) ---")
+!(query 100 ck (: $p (B) $tv))
+
+; The exact shape of upstream's tests/test_stv_implication_derived_ctv.metta,
+; which asserts (query 20 stvRuleKb (: $prf (B x) $tv)) ->
+; (: (aToB a) (B x) (STV 0.6 0.8999998649685302)). Driving it forward instead of
+; backward shows the STV rule form is inert in that direction too, so its test
+; failure is not only the backward-chaining bug.
+!("=== upstream's own stv-implication test shape, forward-chained ===")
+!(compileadd stvRuleKb (: a (A x) (STV 1.0 0.9)))
+!(compileadd stvRuleKb (: aToB (Implication (Premises (A $x)) (Conclusions (B $x))) (STV 0.6 0.9)))
+!("--- forward-chain: derived facts ---")
+!(forward-chain 20 stvRuleKb (sel stvRuleKb (A x)))
+!("--- kb contents after forward-chain ---")
+!(match &kb ($t (stvRuleKb MAIN Nil) $prf $tv) ($t $prf $tv))
+
+!("=== end ===")
diff --git a/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh b/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh

index 0000000..09e12cf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Re-run the ptc-revalidate verdict from a clean clone of this repo.
+#
+#   bash tests/repros/ptc-revalidate/run-verdict.sh
+#
+# Clones the pinned PeTTa and PeTTaChainer from the offline bundles into vendor/, builds PeTTaChainer's
+# own isolated task environment (its .myclaw/Dockerfile), and runs four probes,
+# writing every log under results/ptc-verdict/:
+#
+#   python-unittest.log    PeTTaChainer's Python test suite      (upstream's own)
+#   metta-testsh.log       PeTTaChainer's MeTTa test suite       (upstream's own)
+#   minimal-repro.log      three-line backward-chaining repro    (ours)
+#   rule-tv-encoding.log   STV-vs-CTV rule encoding repro        (ours)
+#   format-a-probe.log     April ProofWriter format-A probe      (ours)
+#
+# The script always exits 0: upstream suites are expected to fail at these pins
+# (that IS the verdict). Read docs/ptc-verdict.md for what the logs should say.
+#
+# Requires: podman (or docker), git, and the sibling deps/ bundle directory. Everything else --
+# SWI-Prolog, Python, janus, uv -- comes from the container image, so the host
+# toolchain does not matter.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
+HERE="$ROOT/tests/repros/ptc-revalidate"
+VENDOR="$ROOT/vendor"
+OUT="$ROOT/results/ptc-verdict"
+
+# PeTTa comes from the repo-wide pins; PeTTaChainer is pinned here, because
+# pins.env deliberately does not vendor it (see its trailing comment).
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+source "$ROOT/pins.env"
+PETTACHAINER_SHA=02a85c63be6a735f50f50e1084a717b3256b8406   # main, 2026-07-20
+DEPS_DIR="${DEPS_DIR:-$ROOT/../deps}"
+
+IMAGE="plnbench-ptc:${PETTACHAINER_SHA:0:7}"
+# PeTTaChainer's .myclaw/petta shim hardcodes /nexus/Dev/OpenCog/PeTTa/run.sh,
+# and its pyproject resolves petta at ../../PeTTa. Mounting the chainer two
+# levels below /nexus/Dev/OpenCog satisfies both without touching either repo.
+CT_PETTA=/nexus/Dev/OpenCog/PeTTa
+CT_CHAINER=/nexus/Dev/OpenCog/work/PeTTaChainer
+
+ENGINE="${CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
+if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
+  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
+  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
+  else echo "ERROR: need podman or docker on PATH." >&2; exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+echo "container engine: $ENGINE"
+
+mkdir -p "$OUT" "$VENDOR"
+
+fetch_bundle () { # bundle sha dir
+  local bundle="$1" sha="$2" dir="$3"
+  [ -f "$bundle" ] || { echo "ERROR: missing dependency bundle: $bundle" >&2; exit 1; }
+  [ -d "$dir/.git" ] || git clone --quiet -b pinned "$bundle" "$dir"
+  git -C "$dir" checkout --quiet "$sha"
+  test "$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$sha" || {
+    echo "ERROR: bundle checkout is not the requested pin: $dir" >&2
+    exit 1
+  }
+  echo "pinned: $dir @ $(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD)"
+}
+fetch_bundle "$DEPS_DIR/PeTTa.bundle" "$PETTA_SHA" "$VENDOR/PeTTa"
+fetch_bundle "$DEPS_DIR/PeTTaChainer.bundle" "$PETTACHAINER_SHA" "$VENDOR/PeTTaChainer"
+
+# --from pins the base image to its fully-qualified name: podman refuses the
+# Dockerfile's short `FROM swipl:9.3.33` when it cannot prompt for a registry.
+echo "building $IMAGE from PeTTaChainer/.myclaw/Dockerfile ..."
+"$ENGINE" build --from docker.io/library/swipl:9.3.33 \
+  -f "$VENDOR/PeTTaChainer/.myclaw/Dockerfile" \
+  -t "$IMAGE" "$VENDOR/PeTTaChainer" > "$OUT/image-build.log" 2>&1 \
+  || { echo "ERROR: image build failed -- see $OUT/image-build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "built: $IMAGE"
+
+# LC_ALL: swipl mangles unicode (and the suites' pass/fail marks) without a
+# UTF-8 locale -- docs/known-issues.md #1.
+# The two named volumes persist uv's cache and its managed CPython across runs.
+# The CPython one is not just a speed-up: .venv lives in the mounted clone and
+# symlinks its interpreter into the container's HOME, so without a persistent
+# HOME every run finds a dangling .venv and rebuilds it from scratch.
+run_in_env () { # workdir command...
+  local workdir="$1"; shift
+  "$ENGINE" run --rm \
+    -e LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 -e LANG=C.UTF-8 \
+    -v "$VENDOR/PeTTa:$CT_PETTA:z" \
+    -v "$VENDOR/PeTTaChainer:$CT_CHAINER:z" \
+    -v "$HERE:/repro:z" \
+    -v plnbench-ptc-uv-cache:/opt/myclaw/uv-cache \
+    -v plnbench-ptc-uv-python:/tmp/myclaw-home/.local \
+    -w "$workdir" \
+    "$IMAGE" bash -lc "$*"
+}
+
+echo
+echo "[1/5] PeTTaChainer Python test suite (upstream's own)"
+run_in_env "$CT_CHAINER" \
+  'uv sync --frozen && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v; echo "PYTHON_UNITTEST_EXIT=$?"' \
+  > "$OUT/python-unittest.log" 2>&1
+grep -E '^(Ran |OK|FAILED|PYTHON_UNITTEST_EXIT)' "$OUT/python-unittest.log" | sed 's/^/  /'
+
+echo
+echo "[2/5] PeTTaChainer MeTTa test suite (upstream's own; several minutes)"
+run_in_env "$CT_CHAINER/pettachainer/metta" \
+  './test.sh; echo "METTA_TESTSH_EXIT=$?"' \
+  > "$OUT/metta-testsh.log" 2>&1
+grep -E '^Summary:|^METTA_TESTSH_EXIT=' "$OUT/metta-testsh.log" | sed 's/^/  /'
+
+echo
+echo "[3/5] minimal backward-chaining repro"
+run_in_env "$CT_CHAINER/pettachainer/metta" \
+  'petta /repro/minimal_repro.metta' \
+  > "$OUT/minimal-repro.log" 2>&1
+sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$OUT/minimal-repro.log" | awk '/^true$/{f=1} f' | sed 's/^/  /'
+
+echo
+echo "[4/5] rule TV encoding repro (STV vs CTV on an Implication)"
+run_in_env "$CT_CHAINER/pettachainer/metta" \
+  'petta /repro/rule_tv_encoding.metta' \
+  > "$OUT/rule-tv-encoding.log" 2>&1
+sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$OUT/rule-tv-encoding.log" | awk '/^true$/{f=1} f' \
+  | grep -v '^(rules ' | sed 's/^/  /'
+
+echo
+echo "[5/5] April ProofWriter format-A probe"
+run_in_env "$CT_CHAINER" \
+  'uv run python /repro/proofwriter_format_a.py --steps 100' \
+  > "$OUT/format-a-probe.log" 2>&1
+sed -n '/^=== encoding=/,/^{$/p' "$OUT/format-a-probe.log" | sed '/^{$/d' | sed 's/^/  /'
+
+echo
+echo "logs written to results/ptc-verdict/ -- compare against docs/ptc-verdict.md"

missing_surfaces.first_read: harness exposes no tool-call transcript; no read timestamp is observable
missing_surfaces.first_verifier: candidate never invoked bin/bench-verify; a verifier it ran directly is invisible

sources.exit: runner wall clock at process reap
sources.first_response: timestamp of the first byte the agent wrote to stdout or stderr
sources.first_write: earliest mtime among files created or modified under code/ during the run

pulse.observed: at least one file under code/ has been created or modified

resolved_identity.cost_missing_surface: this arm runs on a ChatGPT subscription; there is no per-run price to report and an estimate from a price table would not be one
resolved_identity.how_primary_chosen: codex reports one usage block per turn; the last is the total
resolved_identity.resolved_model_missing_surface: codex exec --json reports no SERVER-resolved model id. The value above is the model Codex records having been configured with, read from its session rollout — a harness statement, not a gateway or API echo. Weigh it accordingly.
